prose_rows.claim: Elliptic RP1-circles are uniquely parametrized by a positive real number (the angle): its group-theoretic content, that an elliptic element is conjugate to a rotation and that two elliptic (or central) elements of G~ with the same real angle are conjugate in G~
decls: GX.PSL2.slRot_conj_iff (alpha in (0, pi) is a complete invariant in PSL(2,R))
GX.GTilde.isRotLift_angle (elliptic or central f = h R~(angle f) h^-1)
prose_rows.note: The circle-level statement GX.rp1Iso_of_angle_eq (HSSingularities) closes with (rp1Iso_iff_conj hf hf').2 (GTilde.exists_conj_of_angle_eq he he' hθ). Central holonomy is included as in HSSingularities (OQ-113 (d)).

prose_rows.claim: Hyperbolic conjugacy classes are uniquely parametrized by a positive real number, the absolute value of their trace
decls: GX.sl_exists_conj_slDiag (SL(2,R): A ~ diag(l, l^-1), |l| > 1, l + l^-1 = tr A)

prose_rows.claim: There are exactly two parabolic conjugacy classes, positive (g x >= x on RP~1) and negative (g x <= x)
decls: GX.GTilde.forall_le_iff_of_toPSL_conj_slUpper (the lift with a fixed point of a conjugate of [[1, s], [0, 1]] is positive iff s < 0)
GX.PSL2.IsParabolic.isConj_iff_forall_le (conjugate iff the lifts with a fixed point are both positive or both negative; the signature of GX.PSL2.IsParabolic.isConj_iff)
prose_rows.note: The positive class is that of [[1, -1], [0, 1]] and the negative one that of [[1, 1], [0, 1]], in the coordinates of GX.RP1 (proj t = [cos pi t : sin pi t]).

prose_rows.claim: hyperbolic RP1-circles of degree 0 are uniquely parametrized by a positive real number

kb_proposals: Conjugacy in SL(2,R) is decided by GX.sl_exists_conj_of_trace_eq: same trace, and the forms slQuad A = det[v | A v] = c x^2 + (d-a) x y - b y^2 both take a positive value. [v | A v] with q(v) = 1 conjugates A to slCompanion (tr A). For the other sign use A^-1 in SL (slQuad_inv) or -A in PSL (slQuad_neg, pslMk_neg).

In G~, an elliptic or central f is h R~(angle f) h^-1 (GX.GTilde.isRotLift_angle). A conjugacy in PSL(2,R) lifts to G~ up to delta^n (GX.GTilde.exists_delta_zpow_of_toPSL_conj), exactly when both elements have fixed points (GX.GTilde.exists_conj_of_toPSL_conj).
The lift with a fixed point of [[1, s], [0, 1]] is positive iff s < 0 (GX.GTilde.forall_le_iff_of_toPSL_slUpper): f 0 = 0, and proj (f (1/2)) = [s : 1] decides the sign through cos(pi f(1/2)).
Pitfall: `first | ring | linear_combination ...` never reaches the second branch, because `ring` that fails falls back to ring_nf with a 'Try this' and does not fail. Use `ring1`.

Pattern: Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.fin_two_induction turns A : SL(2,R) into <!![a, b; c, d], hdet>, so simp evaluates the entries and the determinant is hdet. It avoids the `set b := A 0 1` mismatches of kb/0071.
notes: Self-contained group theory; no sorry, no new hypothesis, no edit outside the file. HSSingularities and the scaffold root need `import GXScaffold.BBS.PSL2NormalForms` (T-bbs-hs-remark-existence). No name of this file is declared in HSSingularities.lean, in GX/ or GXScaffold/ elsewhere, in lean-causal, or (at 06:13) in the parallel QuotientCircle.lean and GammaPElements.lean. HSSingularities' GX.PSL2.trSq_conj is unchanged; GX.sl_trace_conj here is its SL(2,R) form, not a duplicate name. The method: one conjugacy criterion (same trace, positive values of det[v | A v]) gives all three normal forms. The parabolic classes are told apart through G~ (positivity is a conjugacy invariant, GX.GTilde.le_conj_apply), not by a matrix computation.
